clue.text: Meet with dockers to change warning system

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its form, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Union talks with the dockworkers aimed at changing an early-warning procedure on the quayside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' only joins the two groups of fodder; the small word 'to' belongs to the letters being shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke detector is an alarm device that warns occupants of a fire, so it is a domestic warning system.

clue.text: Narcotic den at home is busted

indicators.note: something busted is broken apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police raid a drug den operating out of someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busted' reads as a police raid in the surface, which is exactly the drugs picture the answer belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: Methadone is a synthetic opioid drug, used as a substitute for heroin, so it is a narcotic.

clue.text: Heard to want massage

indicators.note: something heard is caught by the ear, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to want something is to need it

explanation.surface: Someone overhearing a friend say they are desperate for a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work muscles with the hands, pressing and squeezing, which is what a masseur does when giving a massage.

clue.text: Get animated about snazzy fabric

indicators.note: about can mean moved around, so the letters before it are turned this way and that

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone getting excited over a flashy piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamante is material decorated with glittering sequins or artificial gems, so it is a showy, sparkly cloth.

clue.text: I left upset rams without 24D?

definitions.note: an example of the answer to 24-down, signalled by the question mark

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the pair of letters is read from the bottom up
without can mean outside, so the rams word sits around the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A clumsy gardener knocks over some sheep, which trample the flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at 24-down, FLORA: tulips are one example of plant life. A tup is a farmers' word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips are spring-flowering bulbs, so they are an instance of flora, the plant life of a region.

clue.text: Italian chap supporting study is person committed to delivery

indicators.note: in a down clue, something supporting another lies beneath it, so this part comes second

blocks.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
signor is the Italian title for a man, like Mr

explanation.surface: An Italian man backs a piece of research and promises to see it through.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the supporting word sits underneath, so the Italian title comes after the study word.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignor is the party who sends goods, consigning them to a carrier, so they are committed to having them delivered.

clue.text: One supporting old guy's an Arab

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so this letter goes at the bottom

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a guy is a man
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after an elderly fellow turns out to be from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a native of Oman, a country on the Arabian Peninsula, so an Omani is an Arab.

clue.text: This is the clue — take it or leave it

definitions.text: This is the clue — take it or leave it

blocks.clueFragment: This is the clue — take it or leave it
blocks.note: surface reading: a curt setter offering the solver this clue and nothing better
setter's reading: an idiom for a choice with only one real option, named after a Cambridge stable keeper

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hobson hired out horses in Cambridge and insisted customers take the one nearest the door or none at all; his name became the phrase for a non-choice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a situation offering a single option to accept or refuse, exactly the take-it-or-leave-it deal described.

clue.text: Being thus stepmother turned puce

definitions.note: the whole clue describes someone who is quick to anger, an adjective phrase

indicators.note: turned means twisted around, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
puce is a dark reddish-purple, loosely red

explanation.surface: A stepmother so irritable she has gone purple in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: a stepmother turning puce is the picture of being quick-tempered, while the wordplay rearranges her and adds the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is short-tempered flares up easily, and going puce with rage is how such a person looks.

clue.text: Where you might put varnish now!

blocks.note: first meaning: literally, on a fingernail
second meaning: an idiom for immediately, as in paying at once

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes 'now!' sound like an urgent order to paint; it is in fact a separate meaning, as in 'paid on the nail'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail varnish goes on a fingernail, and paying on the nail means paying immediately, so the phrase covers both senses.

clue.text: It was once under a town in Wales

blocks.note: first meaning: a poetic, old-fashioned shortening of beneath
second meaning: a town in the south of Wales near Swansea

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sunken Welsh town; really 'It was once' marks an archaic word for under.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Neath is a poetic contraction of beneath, now dated, and Neath is also a Welsh town in the county borough of Neath Port Talbot.

clue.text: Small daughter cuddles brown bear

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold something in your arms, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A little girl hugging her brown teddy bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown bear' looks like a single animal, but the bear is the definition and brown is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it, and to stand it means the same, as in 'I can't stand him'.

clue.text: Hearing aid? Politician visits a long-term prisoner carrying one

indicators.note: someone who visits goes inside a place, so this piece is placed within another
carrying means holding something within, so the prisoner word holds the numeral

blocks.note: taken as written
MP stands for Member of Parliament
a lifer is someone serving a life sentence
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An MP on a prison visit, meeting a lifer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'hearing aid' is not the deaf person's device but anything that helps sound be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplifier boosts sound so it can be heard more easily, a playful sense of something that aids hearing.

clue.text: Being a tiro one played Clash on the radio

indicators.note: played suggests letters toyed with and moved about, so the short word before it is rearranged
on the radio means broadcast as sound, so the word is used for how it is spoken

blocks.note: the three letters of the word rearranged
a clash is a fight

explanation.surface: A novice musician who performed a song by The Clash on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clash were a British punk band, which makes 'played Clash' look musical. A tiro (or tyro) is a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a newcomer or beginner at something, just as a tiro is a novice.

clue.text: Al leaves Henry with university puritans for comedians

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer present, so those two letters are taken out

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
U is the standard abbreviation for university
moralists preach strict morals, as puritans do
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Al walks out on Henry and the university's prudes to join some comics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Al' looks like a man's name; it is just the two letters removed from the puritans word.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorists are writers or performers who make people laugh, so comedians in the broad sense.

clue.text: Obtain the services of volunteer

blocks.note: first meaning: to engage someone's help or support
second meaning: to sign up for service, especially in the armed forces

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about hiring a volunteer, but it splits into two separate meanings of the same verb.
explanation.definitionFit: You enlist someone's help when you secure it, and you enlist when you join the army of your own accord.

clue.text: Jab trendy old clergyman when lecturer replaces rector

indicators.note: replaces means takes the place of, so one letter is swapped in for another

blocks.note: in means fashionable
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a curate is an assistant parish priest
L is a common abbreviation for lecturer
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A fashionable elderly priest has a vaccination, with a lecturer standing in for the rector.
explanation.definitionFit: To inoculate is to inject a vaccine, and a jab is the informal word for such an injection, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Burn some food in this salt

indicators.note: in places one piece within another, so the food word goes inside

blocks.note: to sear is to scorch or burn the surface
fare is food, as in 'simple fare'

explanation.surface: A cook burning part of the meal while seasoning it with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seasoning beside the food, but an old salt is a seasoned sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced sailor, and a seafarer is someone who travels by sea, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Overwhelms conservative with loads of paper

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
a ream is 500 sheets of paper, and reams means a great deal

explanation.surface: Someone burying a cautious colleague under piles of paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To cream an opponent is a slang way of beating them heavily, so it means to overwhelm or thrash.

clue.text: That girl's tower contains one item that's been in the family for years

definitions.text: item that's been in the family for years

indicators.note: contains means holds within, so the numeral goes inside the pronoun

blocks.note: her is the possessive for that girl
the Roman numeral for one
to loom is to tower over something

explanation.surface: A princess's tower housing a treasured family possession, like something from a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' reads as a noun, a building, but it is the verb meaning to rise high over.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued object passed down through generations of a family.

clue.text: Jenny takes motorway around front of French mountains

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the road piece is placed on either side
front of points to the opening letter of the following word, added at the end

blocks.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with the 1 read as the letter I
a jenny is a female donkey or ass
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A woman named Jenny drives along the motorway towards the French Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny looks like a woman's name but is a female donkey. The M1 is England's London to Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming a single block, such as the Massif Central in France.

clue.text: Make an effort to take top off beer for mate

indicators.note: removing the top of a word means its first letter is dropped

blocks.note: to bother to do something is to make the effort
a half is half a pint of beer

explanation.surface: Advice to a drinker to make the effort to open a bottle for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub, ordering 'a half' means half a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Your other half is your spouse or partner, which is what mate means in the sense of a life partner.

clue.text: Head off to dig hole

indicators.note: with its head off, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: to shovel is to dig or scoop earth

explanation.surface: An order to set off and dig a hole in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole' looks like a pit to dig, but here it is slang for a squalid place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a wretched, dirty dwelling, and calling a place a hole means the same thing informally.

clue.text: Instrument that's made of glass

blocks.note: first meaning: a woodwind instrument played by blowing across a hole
second meaning: a tall narrow drinking glass, as for champagne

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a glass instrument; really the two nouns are separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A flute is both a woodwind instrument and a slender, tall champagne glass.

clue.text: State I'd ignored to find vegetation

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: Florida is a US state
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A traveller skipping a state on a botanical tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the collective term for the plant life of an area, which is what vegetation means.

clue.text: Cornwall has many of these chaps

blocks.note: first meaning: small sheltered bays along a coast
second meaning: old British slang for blokes or fellows

explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the south-west tip of England, famous for its rocky coast. 'Cove' is dated British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Coves are small bays, plentiful on the Cornish coastline, and also an old slang word for fellows.

clue.text: Replacement Eurostar finally moving after alteration

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows
alteration means change, so all the gathered letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A replacement train service finally running after engineering changes to the Eurostar.
explanation.walkthrough: Eurostar is the train through the Channel Tunnel, which makes 'replacement' look like a substitute bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is a substitute standing in for someone or something else, so a replacement.

clue.text: Forges vase and mug without cracks around the edge

indicators.note: without means outside, so the face word goes around the vessel word
around the edge means encircling, so the cracks word goes on both sides

blocks.note: a crack is a sharp loud noise, like a blast
mug is slang for the face
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Pottery that has survived the kiln with no cracks around its rim.
explanation.walkthrough: The vessel sits inside the face word, and the result inside the cracks word. 'Forges' is a plural noun, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Blast furnaces are the huge smelting furnaces of ironworks, and a forge is a furnace or workshop for heating metal.
